blogs.title: Young Adult, Big A1c, Negative Antibodies: When to Stop Calling It Type 1 or Type 2
blogs.description: A practical diagnostic approach to suspected MODY in early-onset diabetes, using this case to review the clues that should trigger reconsideration of the default labels: autosomal dominant family history, absence of ketoacidosis, negative islet autoantibodies, preserved stimulated C-peptide, postprandial hyperglycaemia and glycosuria.

blogs.title: The Type 2 Look-Alike Trap: Why BMI, Triglycerides and Mild Metabolic Features Don’t Exclude MODY
blogs.description: This post would explore the growing phenotypic overlap between MODY and type 2 diabetes, especially as obesity becomes more common in younger patients. It would discuss why clinicians should not let a near-normal or mildly elevated BMI, hypertriglyceridaemia or a 'metabolic syndrome' vibe prematurely close the diagnostic process.

blogs.title: Precision Diabetes in Real Time: How a Genetic Diagnosis Changed Therapy
blogs.description: Using this case as a springboard, this post would examine how confirming HNF1A-MODY can alter management: de-escalating insulin, choosing agents that match the underlying beta-cell defect and weighing sulfonylureas versus GLP-1 receptor agonists. It would focus on the bedside implications of precision medicine rather than genetics for genetics’ sake.

blogs.title: Glycosuria as a Genotype Clue: The Renal Physiology of HNF1A-MODY and Why SGLT2 Inhibitors May Be a Bad Fit
blogs.description: A physiology-driven review of why patients with HNF1A-MODY may spill glucose early because of a reduced renal glucose threshold, and how that same biology raises concern for dehydration and ketoacidosis with SGLT2 inhibitors. The post would connect a classic exam finding to modern prescribing decisions.

blogs.title: From Suspicion to Sequencing: When to Order MODY Testing and How to Interpret a Novel Variant
blogs.description: This post would cover the logistics and nuance of genetic testing in monogenic diabetes: who should get an NGS panel, how tools like the MODY probability calculator help but may not generalise across populations, and how ACMG criteria, segregation data and functional inference can support pathogenicity even when a variant is absent from ClinVar.
